exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 A Trip on the Grand Canal
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Dad, where are we going for the trip this weekend?
Dad: I've booked a boat ride along the Grand Canal near Suzhou.
Mia: The Grand Canal? Isn’t that the longest man-made river in the world?
Dad: That’s right. It runs all the way from Beijing to Hangzhou.
Mia: Why was such a long canal built in the first place?
Dad: Long ago it was used to carry grain and supplies to the north.
Mia: Will we see any old towns along the water?
Dad: Yes, several old trading towns still stand beside the canal.
Mia: That sounds wonderful. I’ll bring my camera to take photos.
Dad: Good idea. Remember, this canal is over two thousand years old.
exercises.translation_cn: 米娅问周末去哪;爸爸订了苏州附近大运河的乘船游;米娅问这是不是世界最长的人工河;爸爸说是,从北京一直到杭州;问当初为何修这么长的运河;爸爸说古时用来向北方运粮和物资;问运河边能否看到古镇;爸爸说还有几座古老的贸易小镇;米娅要带相机拍照;爸爸提醒运河已有两千多年历史。

questions.stem: Where are Mia and her dad going this weekend?
options: On a boat ride along the Grand Canal.
To the seaside for a swim.

questions.stem: What was the canal first used for?
options: Carrying grain and supplies to the north.

questions.stem: What runs all the way from Beijing to Hangzhou?
What will they see beside the canal?
How old is the canal, according to Dad?
options: More than two thousand years old.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The Silk Road
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Silk Road was not one single road but a web of many routes.
It connected China with Europe, reaching cities like Istanbul and Venice.
Silk was the most important good traded along these routes.
Traders also carried tea, porcelain and gold across the land.
More than goods, the Silk Road spread ideas, music and new skills.
exercises.translation_cn: 丝绸之路并非一条路,而是众多路线交织成的网;它连接中国与欧洲,直达伊斯坦布尔和威尼斯;丝绸是这些路线上最重要的贸易品;商人也跨陆运送茶叶、瓷器和黄金;丝绸之路传播的不只是货物,还有思想、音乐和新技艺。

questions.stem: Was the Silk Road a single road?
options: Yes, it was one straight road.
No, it was a single river.
Yes, it was a short path.
No, it was a web of many routes.

questions.stem: Which two western cities did it reach?
What was the most important good traded?
What else did traders carry?
Besides goods, what did the Silk Road spread?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 At the Forbidden City
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Guide: Welcome to the Forbidden City, everyone.
Tom: Wow, it’s huge! How many palaces are there?
Guide: There are about ninety palaces, plus many other halls.
Tom: Why is it called the “Forbidden” City?
Guide: Because long ago ordinary people could not enter without permission.
Lily: When was it built?
Guide: It was built between 1406 and 1420, during the Ming dynasty.
Lily: And who lived here?
Guide: Emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties lived and worked here.
Tom: No wonder millions of people visit it every year!
exercises.translation_cn: 导游欢迎大家来到故宫;汤姆惊叹好大,问有多少宫殿;导游说约九十座宫殿外加许多殿堂;汤姆问为何叫"禁"城;导游说从前普通人未经允许不能入内;莉莉问何时建成;导游说1406至1420年明朝所建;问谁住在这里;导游说明清两朝皇帝在此生活和工作;汤姆说难怪每年有数百万人参观。

questions.stem: About how many palaces are there?
Why is it called the “Forbidden” City?
options: It was always covered in fog.
Ordinary people could not enter without permission.
No one was ever allowed inside.

questions.stem: When was it built?
Who lived and worked there?
options: Emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

questions.stem: How many people visit it every year?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Across the Sea
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Silk Road was not only on land; it also crossed the sea.
Scholars call these sea routes the Maritime Silk Road.
Ships left the southern coast of China carrying porcelain and silk.
They sailed through the Strait of Malacca to reach far-off lands.
By sea, heavy and fragile goods could travel more safely than over mountains.
exercises.translation_cn: 丝绸之路不只在陆上,也跨越海洋;学者把这些海上路线称为海上丝绸之路;船只从中国南方海岸出发,载着瓷器和丝绸;它们穿过马六甲海峡到达遥远的地方;走海路,沉重易碎的货物比翻山越岭更安全。

questions.stem: Where did the Silk Road also go, besides land?
What do scholars call the sea routes?
What did ships carry from southern China?
Which strait did the ships sail through?
Why was the sea route good for fragile goods?
options: They could travel more safely than over mountains.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Why Study History
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Teacher: Why do you think we study history, class?
Anna: I think it helps us understand how the world became what it is.
Teacher: Good point. Anything else, Ben?
Ben: History gives us a sense of who we are.
Teacher: Exactly. And what can we learn from past mistakes?
Anna: We can avoid repeating them in the future.
Ben: It also tells great stories about brave people.
Teacher: True. So is history only about the past?
Anna: No, it also helps us plan for the future.
Teacher: Well said. The past is really a guide for what comes next.
exercises.translation_cn: 老师问大家为什么要学历史;安娜说它帮我们理解世界如何变成今天的样子;老师称赞,问本还有什么;本说历史给我们认同感;老师问能从过去的错误中学到什么;安娜说能避免将来重蹈覆辙;本说历史也讲述勇者的精彩故事;老师问历史是否只关乎过去;安娜说不,它也帮我们规划未来;老师总结说过去其实是未来的指南。

questions.stem: According to Anna, how does history first help us?
options: It helps us earn more money.
It helps us forget the past.
It helps us understand how the world became what it is.

questions.stem: What does history give us, in Ben’s view?
options: A sense of who we are.

questions.stem: What can we do with past mistakes?
options: Avoid repeating them in the future.

questions.stem: Is history only about the past?
options: No, it also helps us plan for the future.
No, it is only about money.

questions.stem: What does the teacher call the past at the end?
options: A guide for what comes next.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Visiting a Historic Site
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone visiting a historic site.
Before you go, read a little about its history and meaning.
When you arrive, look closely and imagine the people who once lived there.
Always follow the rules and never touch the ancient walls or relics.
By respecting these places, we help keep them safe for future visitors.
exercises.translation_cn: 给参观历史遗址者的一个小贴士:出发前先了解一点它的历史和意义;到达时仔细观察,想象曾在此生活的人;务必遵守规则,绝不触碰古老的墙壁或文物;尊重这些地方,就能帮助它们为后来者保存下来。

questions.stem: What should you do before visiting a historic site?
options: Read about its history and meaning.

questions.stem: What should you imagine when you arrive?
options: The people who once lived there.

questions.stem: What must you never touch?
What should you always follow?
How do we keep these places safe?
